title: VPC Egress Governor Terraform Module — consolidated security controls and health checks
creator: Marco Ruiz
description:
Goal: Build a single, composable Terraform module (redwood_vpc_egress_governor) that provides opinionated, auditable security controls for private deployments: security groups, NACLs, private DNS zone attachments, and enforceable egress policies. The module should be reusable across Dedicated and Private deployments, support safe upgrades/migrations from existing smaller modules, and expose health-check primitives for runtime monitoring.

Why: Current infra has multiple overlapping small modules handling egress and DNS which causes drift, inconsistent audit trails, and makes upgrades error-prone. This initiative consolidates controls, reduces operator surface area, and enables observability hooks for the Console.

Scope:
- Terraform module API (variables/outputs) for security groups, stateless/ stateful NACL rules, private DNS zone association, and egress policy rules (port/protocol/CIDR allow-lists and deny-lists).
- Built-in plan-time validations (CIDR constraints, no-0.0.0.0/0 by default) and optional hard-deny guardrails.
- Migration helpers and documented import commands for existing SGs/NACLs/Route53 private zones.
- Exported health-check resources and CloudWatch/Prometheus-compatible metrics hooks for the Console to surface: egress-deny-events, private-dns-resolution-failures, config-drift-detection.
- Integration tests and an example workspace demonstrating Dedicated and Private deployments.

Non-goals: Replace provider-specific features (we’ll keep provider-agnostic layer but initial implementation targets AWS). This module will not implement full RBAC — that remains in the Private control plane.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes a small stable public API (<= 12 top-level variables) and clear outputs: sg_ids, nacl_ids, private_dns_zone_id, policy_summary
Terraform plan for example workspace produces no destructive changes when enabling module with default config
Migration docs include terraform import commands and a tested migration runbook for existing ENG tickets listed in dependencies
Health checks emit metrics/timestamps to a metrics topic or CloudWatch so Console can ingest and show alerts
Module passes automated integration tests in CI across two example VPC layouts (single-AZ test VPC, multi-AZ prod-like VPC)
Security review completed and sign-off recorded in Confluence (security_review_required=true)
design_notes: Module composition: submodules for sg (stateful), nacl (stateless), private_dns (zone association), and egress_enforcer (policy rules + optional lambda deny-logger).
Variables: var_environment, var_allowed_egress_cidrs (list), var_restricted_egress_ports (map protocol->list), var_private_dns_zone_name, var_enable_hard_deny (bool-like string), var_tags
Outputs: sg_ids (list), nacl_ids (list), private_dns_zone_id (string), policy_summary (stringified JSON) — policy_summary for Console display
Defaults: Avoid 0.0.0.0/0; if var_enable_hard_deny='true' then module creates explicit deny NACL entries and a deny-logger (optional).
State migration: include tf import examples, an import helper script (scripts/import_existing_resources.sh) and mapping table to reconcile names/IDs

Observability: provide an optional null_resource + local-exec that publishes a control-plane heartbeat (timestamp) and a small metrics bundle to CloudWatch/Prometheus push gateway. Console will subscribe to these metrics for health dashboards.
Upgrade strategy: patch-minor changes should be backwards compatible with existing variables. Breaking changes require a migration guide and a flag var_enable_v2_mode to opt into new behavior.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module in feature branch behind feature flag and land unit tests (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1482).
2) Deploy example workspace to sandbox VPC and run full integration tests (canary).
3) Coordinate with SRE and Security to run manual migration for one non-production tenant (use import scripts).
4) Gradual rollout to Dedicated staging clusters (monitor Console metrics and alert burn-in), then to production Private clusters using canary routing in rollout policy.
5) After 2 weeks of stable telemetry, deprecate old modules with clear timed migration windows and a final migration sprint.
testing_plan: Unit tests for terraform modules using terratest (Go) covering variable validation and plan checks.
Integration tests that apply the module in two pre-provisioned VPC shapes and validate egress behavior with blackbox network checks.
Regression test to ensure no open 0.0.0.0/0 egress is created by default.
Manual runbook validation: run import helper against a test tenant, validate Console shows updated policy_summary and health metrics.
Security audit: run tfsec + manual review by Security team and record findings in Confluence.
